column1: # This table is the join between what a host calls its software and what NVD
# calls it, and it is where CVE-matching accuracy actually lives. Nothing about
# "openssh-server", "libssl3", or "Mozilla Firefox (x64 en-US)" tells a matcher
# which CPE product it is; only a curated mapping does.
# Names are matched against CveIndex::normalize_name() output: lowercased, with
# parenthesised groups, version tokens, and arch/locale noise removed. So the
#   exact   the whole normalized name must equal the pattern
#   prefix  the normalized name must start with the pattern; longest wins
# Prefix rules are how one entry covers a distro's habit of splitting a product
# across many binary packages (openssh-client, openssh-server, openssh-sftp-server).
# They are also the main false-positive risk in the table, so each one is kept as
# specific as it can be while still covering the family.
# Debian ships the library as libssl<N> and the tools as openssl.
# upstream product. The bare "python" exact rule catches the Windows installer's
# DisplayName once its version token is stripped.
# Deliberately NOT a "mozilla" prefix rule: Mozilla ships Thunderbird too, and
# collapsing both onto firefox would report mail-client CVEs against a browser.
